correctness.rationale: Direction (=>) is a valid reduction: silting-discrete implies 2-silting-finite at B, hence tau-finite via AIR/DIJ bijection, hence rep-finite via Zito plus BMR. Direction (<=) is not proved. Type A claims every Dynkin normal form is derived-discrete, but An with t>=2 triangles (e.g. A5 two-triangle, Cartan det 3) has two cycles, infinite global dimension and det !=1, so it is neither gentle one-cycle nor piecewise-hereditary Dynkin and hence not derived-discrete under Vossieck/BGS; clock condition never checked. Types D/E confuse Bastian-Holm-Ladkani good (Brenner-Butler module) mutation connectivity with full iterated irreducible silting-mutation reachability, and assert without evidence that every End(P) stays finite-type hence tau-finite. Computation over GF(7) multiplicity-free boxes is correctly labeled bounded evidence and cannot replace the finiteness argument.

originality.rationale: TARGET-route headline normalized to literal, equivalent (2-silting-finite/tau-finite endomorphism algebras, relation-extension encoding), and dominance (broader silting-discrete censuses/databases) forms and searched via fused SerpBase/OpenAlex/Crossref/OpenAIRE with full-text escalation. Nearest priors are Zito tau-finite iff rep-finite for cluster-tilted, Buan-Vatne/Bastian-Holm-Ladkani derived classifications with no silting content, Aihara-Honma silting inheritance with no cluster-tilted content, and Chang et al. graded gentle/skew-gentle silting criterion with no cluster-tilted corollary. None states or substantively implies silting-discrete iff rep-finite for cluster-tilted.

value.rationale: The headline is a natural two-sided classification boundary motivated before computation: silting-discreteness versus representation-finiteness for the recognized class of cluster-tilted algebras, with explicit sharpness contrast to rep-finite silting-indiscrete Nakayama algebras. If true and proved it would be independently worth retrieving as an exact structural invariant, not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration.
